proposal.blind_spot: Current metrics show every kernel is DRAM-bound but cannot tell a roofline-optimal streaming kernel (leave it alone) from one stuck at 77-86% DRAM due to insufficient resident warps or memory-level parallelism (tune occupancy/ILP), so the optimizer rewrites kernels that have no removable traffic and regresses them.

rationale.sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustain: HIGH with high DRAM% and minimal bytes -> kernel is at the roofline, avoid algorithmic rewrite (prevents the 0.33x/0.36x regressions); LOW -> increase occupancy via num_warps/block sizing, fewer registers, or grid-stride loops to saturate the bus.
rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH with DRAM% below ~85% -> latency-bound, add memory-level parallelism (vectorized/independent loads, prefetch/num_stages); LOW with high DRAM% -> truly bandwidth-limited, only byte reduction helps, and if traffic is already one read plus one write, do not touch the kernel.
